summary.tldr: Replaces the term “child pornography” with “child sexual abuse and exploitation material” in federal law and updates related Criminal Code rules.
what_it_does: Replaces “child pornography” with “child sexual abuse and exploitation material” in section 163.1 of the Criminal Code and in four other federal Acts.
Keeps the same offences and penalties for making, distributing, possessing, and accessing this material under section 163.1, including the stated minimum and maximum jail terms.
Expands the computer seizure rules so judges can order the deletion of electronic copies of this material, or data that makes it available, from a computer system.
Updates publication bans, offence lists, and related court rules so section 163.1 is treated as a listed sexual offence in several Criminal Code provisions.
Keeps ongoing proceedings valid after the law takes effect, and says old references to “child pornography” in those proceedings read as the new term.
Starts on the first anniversary of royal assent.
summary.background: The bill says the Criminal Code term “child pornography” is replaced with “child sexual abuse and exploitation material.” It also makes related changes in other Acts.
